definition: JOONE (Java Object Oriented Neural Engine) is a component based neural network framework built in Java.
details: JOONE (Java Object Oriented Neural Engine) is a component based neural network framework built in Java.

explainer.lead: JOONE (Java Object Oriented Neural Engine) is a component-based neural network framework built in Java. It gave Java developers a structured way to assemble neural networks from reusable components.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolkit for building neural networks out of ready-made parts, written for the Java programming language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compose neural networks from its components rather than writing everything from scratch; the framework is a historical tool, so modern practice typically uses newer libraries.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition or formula is given for JOONE beyond its description as a component-based neural network framework in Java.

explainer.example: A developer assembles a network by connecting JOONE components for layers and training rather than coding those pieces manually.
